They were {{ls}}candalized.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Chry{{ls}}. ho. 49, in Mt.''}}This {{ls}}candal ro{{ls}}e partly of enuy of his equals by birth, who reputing them {{ls}}elues as good as he, tooke {{ls}}korne to be taught of him. Wherevpon Chri{{ls}}t {{ls}}aith, ''A Prophet is not without honour but in his owne countrie'': {{ls}}ignifying (as it is plaine in Luke) {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 4, 25.''}}the malice and enuy of the Iewes his countrie men in refu{{ls}}ing him ''(Io. 1''.) and that the Gentils would more e{{ls}}teeme of him.

''5. He could not.''] It is {{ls}}aid that he could not worke miracles there, not meaning that he was not able, but that on their part there wanted apt di{{ls}}po{{ls}}ition to receiue them. And therfore he would not of cōgruity worke there, vvhere their incredulity vvas {{ls}}o great, that it vvould not haue profited them. And for this cau{{ls}}e he {{ls}}aith {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Marc. 5, 36.''}}els where to them that wil {{ls}}ee and enioy his miracles, ''Only beleeue''.

''9. Not two coates.''] He forbiddeth {{ls}}uperfluites, and to careful proui{{ls}}ion of bodily things, when they are about Gods {{ls}}eruice in gaining {{ls}}oules. And for the contrariety that {{ls}}eemeth here and in S. Matthew{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 10.''}}, vnder{{ls}}tand that there he forbiddeth them to carie rod or {{ls}}taffe to defend them {{ls}}elues, here he permitteth a vvalking rod or {{ls}}taffe to leane and {{ls}}tay vpon: there he forbiddeth {{ls}}hoes to couer al the foote, {{ls}}uch as we vveare: here he permitteth {{ls}}andals, that is {{ls}}uch as had {{ls}}oles only, which the poore commonly vvare in Ievvry, and novv {{ls}}ome religious men. See S. Augu{{ls}}tins opinion ''li. 2 c. 30 de con{{ls}}en{{ls}}u Euang. to. 4.''

''13. With oile.''] In the wordes of the commi{{ls}}sion oile is not mentioned, and yet it is certaine by this their v{{ls}}ing of oile, that either Chri{{ls}}t did then appoint them to v{{ls}}e it, or they might take it vp of them {{ls}}elues, by vertue of the general commi{{ls}}sion.

''13. With Oile.'') By this it is cleere that not only the Apo{{ls}}tles or other may haue power to worke miracles, by their only word and inuocation of Chri{{ls}}ts name, but al{{ls}}o by application of creatures: which creatures al{{ls}}o haue a miraculous medicinal vertue to heale di{{ls}}ea{{ls}}es.

{{c|''The ma{{ls}}ters of Hieru{{ls}}alem comming {{ls}}o farre to carpe him 6 he chargeth with traditions, partly friuolous, 9 partly al{{ls}}o contrarie to Gods commaundements. 14 And to the people he yeldeth the rea{{ls}}on of that which they carped, 17 and againe to his di{{ls}}ciples, {{ls}}hewing the ground of the Iewi{{ls}}h wa{{ls}}hing (to witte, that meates otherwi{{ls}}e defile the {{ls}}oule) to be fal{{ls}}e. 24 But by and by among the Gentils, in a vvoman he findeth vvonderful faith, vpon her therfore he be{{ls}}tovveth the crumme that {{ls}}he a{{ls}}ked, 32 returning (becau{{ls}}e the time of the Gentils vvas not yet come) to the Ievves vvith the loafe. 32 Where he {{ls}}hevveth his compa{{ls}}sion tovvardes mankind {{ls}}o deafe and dumme, 36 and of the people is highly magnified.''}} {{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=7|verse=1}}}}{{sc|Nd}} there a{{ls}}{{ls}}emble together vnto him the Phari{{ls}}ees and certaine of the Scribes, comming from Hieru{{ls}}alem.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 15, 1.''}} {{verse|chapter=7|verse=2}}† And vvhen they had {{ls}}een certaine of his di{{ls}}ciples eate bread vvith {{sup|‖}} common hands, that is, not vva{{ls}}hed, they blamed them. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=3}}† For the Phari{{ls}}ees and al the Ievves, vnles they often vva{{ls}}h their hands, eate not, holding the tradition of the Auncients: {{verse|chapter=7|verse=4}}† and from the market, vnles they be vva{{ls}}hed, they eate not: and many other things there be that vvere deliuered vnto them to ob{{ls}}erue, the vva{{ls}}hings of cuppes and cru{{ls}}es, and of bra{{ls}}en ve{{ls}}{{ls}}els & beddes. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=5}}† And the Phari{{ls}}ees and Scribes a{{ls}}ked him, Why do not thy di{{ls}}ciples vvalke according to the tradition of the Auncients, but they eate bread vvith common hands? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=6}}† But he an{{ls}}vvering, {{ls}}aid to them, Wel did E{{ls}}ay Prophecie of you hypocrites, as it is vvritten, ''This people honoureth me '' {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ They that {{ls}}ay well or teache and preache well, or haue Chri{{ls}}t and his word in their mouth, and liue naughtily, be touched in this place.}}∷ ''with their lippes, but their hart is farre from me''.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''E{{ls}}a. 29, 13.''}} {{verse|chapter=7|verse=7}}† ''and in vaine doe they vvor{{ls}}hip me, teaching doctrines {{sup|‖}} precepts of men''.<noinclude>{{rh|||For}}</noinclude>
